title: The liturgy renewed (Sacrosanctum Concilium)
hookLine: full and active participation, and the Mass in the people's languages
tomorrow: The universal call to holiness (Lumen Gentium 5)

cards: The priest says, The Lord be with you. And a whole church answers back, out loud, in the language they argue and shop and text in. It sounds so ordinary that it's easy to miss what a change it was.

Some Catholics still remember Masses where the server gave the responses in Latin and the people prayed quietly on their own. The council's document on worship set out to change that. Today: the liturgy renewed.

teach.b: The document is called Sacrosanctum Concilium, from its first Latin words, this sacred council. Three ideas run through it. First, participation.

The council said the Church earnestly desires that all the faithful be led to a full, conscious and active participation in the liturgy, and that this isn't a favor granted to them but their right and duty by baptism.
It pointed to Saint Peter, in the Douay-Rheims: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation." The people at Mass are not an audience. Second, what taking part looks like.
The council listed it: acclamations, responses, psalms, antiphons and songs, gestures and posture, and, at the proper times, a reverent silence. Silence counts. Kneeling counts.
Latin was to be kept in the Latin rites, and the mother tongue could be given a larger place, in the readings, the prayers and the chants, with the bishops deciding how.
Catholics still differ over how far the changes should have gone, and some prefer the older form in Latin; the council's own text asked for both Latin and the people's languages to have a place.

But the center of the document isn't the language question. It's the picture of a church where nobody is only watching. The psalm says it in the plural: "O magnify the Lord with me; and let us extol his name together."

how: At Mass, Catholics answer the priest's greetings, say or sing the Gloria, Creed, Holy and Lamb of God together, stand, sit and kneel at set moments, and keep silence at times; the Mass is celebrated in local languages and, in some places, in Latin.

games.q: the liturgy renewed — tap the pairs.

s: the council abolished Latin in the Mass
it said Latin was to be kept and the mother tongue given a larger place.
the council listed silence as a way of taking part
alongside songs and responses, it named a reverent silence at the proper times.
the council called participation a favor granted to the people
it called it their right and duty by baptism.

games.q: you're drafting the council's text. in your parish, the people at Mass only watch. what do you ask for?
o: leave things as they are; watching is enough.
full, conscious and active participation by all the faithful.
let only the choir sing on the people's behalf.
games.why: Sacrosanctum Concilium asked for full, conscious and active participation by all, calling it their right and duty by baptism.

practice: Bring one of the sung parts of Mass to mind, the Holy, Holy, Holy, the Lamb of God, the Alleluia, or simply And with your spirit, and hum it under your breath or just hear it inside. Notice where you'd usually go quiet.
If you go to Mass, let that be the part you join next time, even softly; if you don't, think of one place in your week where you only watch, and could join.

wordCard.voice: Sacrosanctum Concilium. Vatican Two's document on worship, calling all the faithful to full, conscious and active participation in the liturgy. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: all of us, taking part. Nobody at Mass is only an audience. See you tomorrow.
